content:
maya: Heads-up — ran into some odd tail-latency on prod when the eviction daemon started favoring recently-touch metadata over SLA weights. Can we sync on what signals should win for 'stale' pages?
liam: ugh, saw that in canary too. looks like the stale tag TTL we added is being shadowed by raw last_access recency. :confused:
sasha: is this the case where tenant A has high SLA weight but low request rate so pages sit idle and then get evicted too eagerly?
maya: exactly. tenant A paid for p99 latency guarantees, but eviction decided those idle pages were low hotness and pushed them out — causing big recompute latencies when a burst hit.
oliver: my read: eviction_score pipeline currently mixes three signals: access_recency, reuse_count, and global_usage_window. SLA_weight is applied as a multiplier at the very end. ordering matters.
oliver: proposal: compute a baseline score from micro-telemetry, then apply an SLA-aware bias BEFORE thresholding, not after. e.g.
```
// pseudo
base = norm(access_age) * w_age + norm(reuse_count) * w_reuse
bias = log(1 + sla_weight) * sla_coeff
evict_score = base - bias - ttl_penalty
```
Then sort by evict_score ascending.
jen: sounds reasonable. how do we set sla_coeff? ops needs something safe for multi-tenant bursty workloads.
liam: start with conservative coeff (0.5) and run canary on a subset of hosts with per-tenant telemetry. collect: p50/p95/p99 for cold-start after eviction, plus overall eviction rate per tenant.
sasha: telemetry caveat: current traces only emit aggregated host-level hotset sizes. we need tenant-scoped eviction-sources and a histogram of post-evict cold-latency. otherwise we can't attribute.
maya: agree. add two metrics: tenant.evictions_per_min and tenant.post_eviction_latencies{p50,p95,p99}. also emit eviction_reason tag (stale_ttl, low_reuse, admission_pressure).
evictor-bot: deploy plan created: rollout/evict-bias-v1 -> 10% hosts -> 1h -> 25% -> 3h -> 100% if metrics ok. link: https://deploys.internal/evict-bias-v1 :gear: 
oliver: another interface issue: where should TTL live? allocator currently owns page descriptors; eviction controller owns scoring. If TTL stays inside allocator, we add a small API: allocator.get_page_meta(page_id) -> {last_access, reuse_count, ttl_state, tenant_id}. keep the policy logic centralized in eviction controller.
sasha: +1, but watch locking overhead. do bulk reads for scoring window, avoid per-page RPC to allocator.
maya: for correctness, we should also add a 'tenant_panic' override: if tenant has active incident or 'latency-burst' flag, treat bias as infinite (no evict unless OOM). admin toggle via console.
jen: ops question: rollback strategy? can we auto-revert on SLO regression?
oliver: yes — the rollout job will monitor tenant.post_eviction_latencies and host.eviction_rate; if p99 increases > 20% for any SLA-weighted tenant during a check window, auto-revert the config on that host and alert #incidents.
liam: small UX note: in Console add slider for sla_coeff and radio for policy placement (pre-threshold, post-threshold). keep default conservative.
maya: next steps: oliver to PR eviction_score change (+unit tests + perf bench), sasha to add telemetry + histograms, jen to wire deploy job alarm thresholds, liam to update console knobs. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up after the first canary.
maya: thanks all :+1:
jen: adding runbook snippet for emergency revert: `curl -XPOST /admin/host/<host>/config -d '{"evict_bias_enabled":false}'` — will post to #eng-oncall.
oliver: one final thought — prefer additive bias in score space (not multiplicative) so we can reason about marginal impact analytically. will include derivation in PR.
maya: awesome. putting TODOs in the issue tracker now.
sasha: can someone add a short test harness that simulates burst on cold tenant after eviction? that'll make telemetry thresholds less guesswork.
maya: on it.
